:::{#cor-entropy-quantization-diverges}
#### Entropy of a quantized random variable grows without bound

In the setting of @thm-entropy-quantization,
the [entropy](#def-entropy) of the quantized variable tends to $\infty$ as the bin width shrinks:

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} \to \infty \quad \text{as } \Delta \to 0.$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-entropy-quantization,
$\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \entropyf{X}$ as $\Delta \to 0$.
Moving $\log \Delta$ to the other side,

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} = \paren{\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta} - \log \Delta.$$

The first quantity on the right tends to $\entropyf{X}$,
not $\pm\infty$:
the [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous) and $0$ outside a [bounded](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-bounded) [interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/chapters/sets.html#def-interval),
so $-\p(X=x) \log \p(X=x)$ is continuous there, with the convention $0 \log 0 = 0$,
and a [continuous function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous) has an [integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral) over a bounded interval.
Also, $-\log \Delta \to \infty$ as $\Delta \to 0$,
so $\entropyf{X^\Delta} \to \infty$.

:::
